title: Climate Change Could Wipe Out Japan's Ski Resorts
paragraphs: Japan could be left with only seven fully operational ski resorts if nothing is done to reduce global warming, according to a new study.

Japan's ski resorts are famous for having high-quality powder snow, which brings many tourists to the country during the winter ski season. At present, there are around 470 ski resorts operating in Japan.
But according to researchers in Japan, most of those resorts would have to close if the world's average temperature increases by 4 degrees Celsius from pre-industrial levels.

The research team looked at 349 ski resorts across the country. Using data from the Japan Meteorological Agency, they created snow cover simulations over a 60-year period in which average temperatures increased by 2 degrees or 4 degrees above pre-industrial levels.

An increase of 4 degrees would mean almost nothing was done to reduce global warming. In this scenario, just seven resorts would be able to stay fully operational, while 26 could be partially operational — meaning only their higher slopes would have enough snow.
In the 2-degree temperature increase scenario, 53 ski resorts would be fully operational and 108 would be partially operational.
Two degrees of warming above pre-industrial levels was the upper limit agreed to in 2015 under the Paris Agreement.
The researchers said their findings show how important it is to stop global warming to protect Japan's ski culture.

However, Nao Yoshizawa, one of the study authors, told The Asahi Shimbun that even if global warming is reduced, many areas will have to adapt to the changing environment and consider whether they will be able to rely on the ski industry.
